name: Overberg

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Syrah, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo, Dolcetto and Merlot fully without cooking off their freshness.
Syrah sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Sauvignon Blanc is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely. Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 7°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
